title: Separable splitting of a geometrically diagonal coalgebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $k^s\subset\bar k$ be a separable closure inside an algebraic closure [def-pd-separable-closure, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a $k$-coalgebra. This means a $k$-vector space with linear maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\epsilon:C\to k$ satisfying coassociativity and the two counit identities. Tensor products have the meaning in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. An element $c$ is group-like when $\Delta(c)=c\otimes c$ and $\epsilon(c)=1$. For a field extension $F/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], write $C_F=F\otimes_k C$ with its scalar-extended coalgebra structure. If $C_{\bar k}$ has a $\bar k$-basis consisting of group-like elements, then the set of all group-like elements of $C_{k^s}$ is a $k^s$-basis of $C_{k^s}$. No finite-dimensionality assumption on $C$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)–(d), printed pp.237–238: the coalgebra argument that geometrically diagonal coalgebras are coétale and split over a separably closed field; Corollary 12.19, p.238.

proof.text: Put $K=k^s$, $L=\bar k$, and $V=K\otimes_kC$. Here $K$ is separably closed by [def-pd-separable-closure], and $L$ is an algebraic closure also of $K$: every element is algebraic already over $k$, and $L$ is algebraically closed. The maps $a\otimes(b\otimes c)\mapsto ab\otimes c$ and $a\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes c)$ identify $L\otimes_KV$ with $C_L$ and respect the coalgebra maps on pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Denote its given group-like basis by $(g_i)_{i\in I}$. Fix any $v\in V$. By [lem-sfb-coalgebra-finite-subcoalgebra] choose a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra $D\subset V$ containing $v$.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: The inclusions $D\subset V$ and $D\otimes_KD\subset V\otimes_KV$ stay injective after tensoring by $L$: use [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] for each inclusion. Thus $W=L\otimes_KD$ is a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra of $C_L$. For a finite basis of $D$, each of its images has finite support in $(g_i)$; their union is a finite set $S_0$, and $W\subset\operatorname{span}_L\{g_i:i\in S_0\}$. These tensor inclusions may also be checked by extending a vector-space basis of $D$ to one of $V$.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: Let $\lambda_i:C_L\to L$ be the $i$th basis coordinate. For $w=\sum_i a_ig_i\in W$, the subcoalgebra condition gives $(1\otimes\lambda_i)(\Delta w)\in W$, whereas the group-like formula gives $(1\otimes\lambda_i)(\Delta w)=a_ig_i$. If $a_i\ne0$, this implies $g_i\in W$. Consequently $W$ has basis exactly $(g_i)_{i\in S}$, where $S=\{i\in S_0:g_i\in W\}$. No finite generation assumption on $C$ or $V$ was used. This is a coordinate calculation using tensor bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-coalgebra-dual-base-change] to $D$ over $K$, and put $A=D^*$. Its scalar comparison identifies $L\otimes_KA$ with $W^*$. Evaluation on the basis from step 3 identifies $W^*$ with $L^S$ as algebras: $(fh)(g_i)=f(g_i)h(g_i)$ and the convolution unit evaluates to $\epsilon(g_i)=1$. The inverse sends $(a_i)$ to $\sum_i b_ig_i\mapsto\sum_i a_ib_i$. Thus $L\otimes_KA$ is commutative and reduced. The map $A\to L\otimes_KA$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, is injective: choose a $K$-linear functional $\ell:L\to K$ with $\ell(1)=1$ by extending $\{1\}$ to a basis; $\ell\otimes1_A$ is a linear retraction. Therefore commutators and nilpotents in $A$ vanish, and $A$ is a commutative reduced finite-dimensional $K$-algebra.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], $A$ is Artinian. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product]: the maximal-ideal set $M$ is finite and the canonical quotient map is $A\cong\prod_{m\in M}E_m$, with $E_m=A/m$ a field. This is also a $K$-algebra isomorphism, since each component has the quotient scalar structure. Each $E_m$ is finite-dimensional over $K$: the images of a finite basis of $A$ span it. If $A=0$, the set $M$ is empty, as permitted by the cited statement.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: The finite-product tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product], together with swapping tensor factors, identifies $A\otimes_KL$ with $\prod_{m\in M}(E_m\otimes_KL)$. The swap is given by $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$, with the same formula as inverse, by tensor bilinearity. The product comparison is multiplicative on pure tensors and preserves $1$, hence is an algebra isomorphism. Each factor $E_m\otimes_KL$ is reduced: embed it additively into the product by zero in all other coordinates; this insertion preserves multiplication, so a nonzero nilpotent in a factor would give one in the product, contradicting step 4. By [lem-pc-finite-extension-tensor-algebraic-closure-reduced-separable], applied to the finite extension $E_m/K$ and the algebraic closure $L/K$, each $E_m/K$ is separable. Since $K$ is separably closed, [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial] identifies each $E_m$ with $K$. Thus $A\cong K^M$ as $K$-algebras.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: For each $m\in M$, the $m$th coordinate of $A\cong K^M$ is an algebra homomorphism $p_m:A\to K$. By [lem-sfb-finite-coalgebra-dual-base-change], it is evaluation at a unique group-like $d_m\in D$. The functionals $p_m$ form a basis of $A^*$: for $\alpha\in A^*$, write $\alpha=\sum_m\alpha(e_m)p_m$, where $e_m$ are the coordinate idempotents transported to $A$. The evaluation isomorphism $D\cong A^*$ therefore says $(d_m)$ is a basis of $D$. Under the coalgebra inclusion $D\subset V$ these remain group-like. In particular the arbitrary $v$ of step 1 lies in their span; hence all group-like elements of $V$ span $V$. If $D=0$, both coordinate families are empty and this argument is vacuous.

source.place: Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238, with the finite-coalgebra argument of pp.174–175 and 237; explicit geometric-subcoalgebra reduction

proof.text: Finally every group-like $h\in V$ maps to one of the geometric basis elements $g_i$. Indeed write its image as a finite sum $\sum_i a_ig_i$ in $C_L$. Comparing the $(i,j)$ coordinates of $\Delta h=h\otimes h$ gives $a_i^2=a_i$ and $a_ia_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, while $\epsilon(h)=1$ gives $\sum_i a_i=1$. Over the field $L$, exactly one coefficient is $1$ and all others are $0$. The scalar map $V\to L\otimes_KV$ is injective by the same retraction $\ell\otimes1_V$ used in step 4, so distinct group-like elements have distinct images $g_i$. A finite $K$-linear relation between them becomes a relation between distinct elements of the $L$-basis $(g_i)$ and has all coefficients zero. Thus they are independent as well as spanning, which proves the required basis statement, including $C=0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q133-8f7b4f613 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's 8 steps, both new unsplit nodes, every cited statement, and Milne iAG2017 Thm 12.18 (b)-(d) pp.237-238, Prop 4.7 p.86 and C_V p.175. The item statement is true and does not assume finite dimension. Steps 1-3 reduce to a finite subcoalgebra D of C_{k^s}, and show by the coordinate contraction (1⊗λ_i)Δw=a_i g_i that W=L⊗D has a group-like basis. Step 4 replaces Milne's antipode argument (b)⇒(c), which an arbitrary coalgebra cannot use: θ_L and evaluation give L⊗A≅L^S as algebras, and the retraction ℓ⊗1 makes A commutative and reduced. Steps 5-6 use the Artinian, reduced-Artinian product, finite tensor-product, reduced-tensor separability and sepclosed-trivial nodes, with every hypothesis checked: commutativity from step 4, L is an algebraic closure of K, factors are reduced via the multiplicative insertion. Step 7 follows Milne (c)⇒(d) through the character/group-like bijection of the duality node. Step 8 is a correct coefficient comparison for independence; the existing leaf lem-sfb-coalgebra-group-like-independent would also do (advisory). The new nodes are true (fundamental theorem of coalgebras; finite duality with base change). Small cases checked: D=0 gives A=0 with no characters and no group-likes; a noncommutative A is allowed. Neither node is a clause of the item or a duplicate: rg -L over dag/nodes found no such node, and Mathlib Coalgebra/Convolution and GroupLike are no leaf for either. Accepted tool_use: lem-pc-finite-extension-tensor-algebraic-closure-reduced-separable (generic field criterion). No SGA, no route change, no fixes.
